verdict.rationale: Paddle documents first-party checkout acceptance: Paddle.js overlay checkout needs only minimal frontend code, and a Next.js starter kit includes an integrated checkout. A solo founder also reports taking payments through Paddle. Nothing in the pack shows how long it takes from signup to accepting a live payment, and sandbox explicitly cannot accept real payments. missing for 10: evidence of live-account onboarding or approval time (going live within a day), explicit card-payment method documentation, independent hands-on report of time-to-first-payment.

support.subject: As a founder, I can accept an online card payment within a day of signing up

citations.quote: Overlay checkout lets you present customers with an overlay that handles all parts of the checkout process — minimal frontend coding required.
Add a checkout to your app or website using Paddle.js to let customers buy one-time products and sign up for a subscriptions.

Production-ready Next.js SaaS starter kit with Paddle Billing, Supabase auth, and Vercel deployment. Includes a localized pricing page, integrated checkout, and customer subscription management screens.
I use Paddle for taking payments for a paid Chrome extension and they've been great with me.
